mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months indicates the Federal Reserve is shifting from tightening to easing, which lowers discount rates and increases the present value of expected equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the federal funds rate above 5.25% triggers a risk-off reaction in equity markets, compressing discount rates and reducing the present value of expected equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in rate hike periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a strengthening labor market, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain or cut rates, which lowers discount rates and increases the present value of expected equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in strengthening labor markets are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the number of payroll jobs exceeding 50,000 signals a robust labor market, which reduces the risk premium on equities and compresses discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in job growth periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the number of payroll jobs below 200,000 indicates softening labor market conditions, prompting the Federal Reserve to hold or cut rates, which lowers discount rates and increases the present value of expected equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in job contraction periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in the Industrial Production index above 105 signals a strengthening supply-side capacity, which reduces the risk premium on equities and compresses discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in capacity expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) below 215 indicates easing inflationary pressures, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain or cut rates, which lowers discount rates and increases the present value of expected equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in CPI easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 220 signals persistent inflationary pressures, prompting the Federal Reserve to raise rates, which compresses discount rates and reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in CPI inflation periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
